title: Microsoft Teams: manage call groups from Teams on Mobile
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, Microsoft's tenant notice and the cited documentation. The mobile rollout, Teams Phone requirement, existing calling-policy controls and admin routes agree with those sources.

claims.claim: The notice describes changing a call group before this feature as requiring the desktop.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Risk assessment; rationale: cost and impact
claims.claim: The notice makes the mobile feature available to users with a Teams Phone licence.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Learn says users must be assigned a Microsoft Teams Phone licence to set up and use call sharing and group call pickup.
claims.quote: Users must be assigned a Microsoft Teams Phone license to set up and use call sharing and group call pickup.

claims.claim: The mobile capability is included under the existing Teams Phone entitlement.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The notice names no other licence, meter or charge for the mobile experience.
claims.quote: This feature is available to users with a Teams Phone license and uses the existing calling policy that controls call groups.

claims.claim: The notice lists no admin prerequisites beyond the stated calling policy and licence.
claims.quote:
No admin action is required before rollout.

Manage call groups on Mobile uses the same controls as the desktop experience.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Call groups share incoming calls with colleagues who can answer while the user is unavailable.
claims.quote: The call sharing and group call pickup features of Microsoft Teams let users share their incoming calls with colleagues so that the colleagues can answer calls that occur while the user is unavailable.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The calling-policy control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Inbound calls can be routed to call groups.
claims.quote:
select Voice > Calling policies.
2. Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit.
3. Make the changes that you want

Inbound calls can be routed to call groups

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowCallGroups $true enables call groups through a Teams calling policy.
claims.quote:
[-Identity] <string>
[-AllowCallGroups <boolean>]

Enables the user to configure call groups in the Microsoft Teams client and that inbound calls should be routed to call groups.

claims.where: controls[0].note; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The existing calling policy governs mobile call groups, and a user with call groups turned off cannot use the mobile feature.
claims.quote: If call groups are turned off for a user in their calling policy, they won't be able to use the feature on Mobile.

claims.claim: Calling policies can be assigned to individual users or groups.
claims.quote: Assigns a specific Teams Calling Policy to a user, a group of users, or sets the Global policy instance.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The admin route is Users > Manage users > user > Voice > Call answering rules > Ring user's devices > Also allow > Group call pickup > Manage call group.
claims.quote:
go to Users > Manage users and select a user.
On the user details page, go to the Voice tab.
Under Call answering rules
Ring user's devices and select Group call pickup from the Also allow dropdown.
Select Manage call group

claims.claim: Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity <user principal name> -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets <array of sip addresses> sets the user's group membership and ring order.
claims.quote:
$cgm = @("sip:user2@contoso.com","sip:user3@contoso.com")
Set-CsUserCallingSettings -Identity user1@contoso.com -CallGroupOrder InOrder -CallGroupTargets $cgm

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls table
claims.claim: CallGroupTargets must specify the full membership and overwrites the current membership.
claims.quote: The members of the Call Group. You need to always specify the full set of members as the parameter value. What you set here will overwrite the current call group membership.

claims.claim: The second control edits an individual user's group rather than enabling or disabling the Mobile screen.
claims.quote: Configures calling settings for a specified user or resource account, including call forwarding, simultaneous ringing, call groups, delegation, and other call-handling options.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and .api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate UI or API switch specifically for call group management on Teams on Mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile Manage call group separate policy switch disable mobile call groups; Teams mobile call groups Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy. Read call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup, teams-calling-policy, settings-policies-reference and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; no separate mobile switch.

claims.claim: The available sources describe no new identity or permission for mobile call group management.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Manage call group mobile permissions identity. Read MC1552390, call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup and teams-calling-policy; no new identity or permission described.

claims.claim: The cited Learn call group page has no mobile-specific management steps at the time of this check.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Mobile manage call group Settings Calling Teams Phone license. Read call-sharing-and-group-call-pickup in full: admin-center and PowerShell management steps, but no mobile management procedure.

claims.claim: Be immediately forwarded sends calls onwards without ringing the user's own devices.
claims.quote: Be immediately forwarded so that calls to the user don't ring their devices.

claims.claim: A call group can have up to 25 users.
claims.quote: Each call group can have up to 25 users.

claims.claim: A user can own only one call group.
claims.quote: A user can only own one call group.

claims.claim: Adding more than five members automatically switches ring order to Everyone at once.
claims.quote: If you add more than five members to a call group, the ring order automatically switches to "Everyone at once."

claims.claim: The call group owner and members must be in Teams Only deployment mode.
claims.quote: Users, the call group owner, and members of the call group must be in Teams Only deployment mode.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn directs admins disabling call groups to clean up relationships in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect routing.
claims.quote: When you turn off call groups for users, you must clean up the call group relationships for users in the Teams admin center to avoid incorrect call routing.

claims.claim: Use unanswered settings and Send to voicemail for Routing for PSTN calls take precedence over call group forwarding settings.
claims.quote: If Use unanswered settings or Send to voicemail is used, either of these settings will have precedence over other call forwarding settings like call forwarding with simultaneous ringing to delegate, call groups, or call forwarding.

claims.claim: The low cost rating reflects the documented preparation work rather than a newly published mobile licence or meter.
